text:
maria: Heads-up — after the telemetry v2 canary landed (small percent in EU), consoles are seeing slow paints on the heatmap and timeseries widgets. Repro on staging and a few prod traces.
kevin: uhoh. any error spikes in Sentry or trace spans?
maria: Sentry is mostly noise-free but span breakdowns show main-thread parse + eval jumps from ~30ms -> 220ms during initial chart hydration. flamegraphs attached in thread (short).
jonah: is this the telemetry bundle change that inlined the probe micro-collector?
maria: yep. telemetry client moved from dynamic import to eager import to fix lost events. that bumped chunk size and changed execution order.
priya: can you paste the bundle size diff?
maria: from sourcemap delta: +92KB gzipped for dashboard entry. also saw extra 3k evals of `augmentTelemetry()` per page load.
sam: 92KB sounds small, but if it forces a hot path parse before widget code, that can blow LCP.
alex: also check our prefetch order — the prefetch priority got shuffled with the new import, maybe prefetching telemetry before viz.
maria: exactly — on canary we see telemetry init fired before kvcache bootstrap, which forces chart to wait on main thread longer.
taylor: what about routing/quota side? any fallout from client-side rate-limiting calling back to /v1/telemetry?
maria: we saw a small spike in telemetry ingestion, but more importantly some clients hit an internal client-side queue limit and blocked until backpressure drained.
kevin: blocking queue is concerning. sounds like the telemetry init is synchronous-ish and throttles event loop. can we repro with `NODE_OPTIONS=--prof` on staging to get more detail?
jonah: I'm worried about toggling dynamic import back and reordering prefetch. rolling back telemetry change seems lower risk than rolling back whole canary.
priya: can we do quick mitigation: lazy-init telemetry until after first paint? that would keep events but avoid blocking.
maria: I tried `requestIdleCallback(() => initTelemetry())` in a branch — staging paint improved but we lost some early events. tradeoff.
sam: alternative: keep eager import but move the heavy augmentor to a microtask that yields once. e.g., `queueMicrotask(() => heavyAugment())`. probably less impact than parse ordering.
alex: also check our CDN chunk ordering headers — we can bump `rel=prefetch` ordering to prefer viz bundle before telemetry.
taylor: for immediate, can we shrink telemetry import surface with a tiny wrapper that defers heavy ops? then revert in two hours if green.
kevin: let's do quick A/B: canary A keeps telemetry eager, canary B moves augment to microtask and defers submodules. run for 10% each. monitor LCP and trace main-thread parse.
priya: I'll prepare a small canary deploy config and a rollout plan (10/10/restore). include telemetry metrics and console LCP SLO in rollout dashboard.
jonah: if microtask approach fails, revert to lazy-init. prioritize not regressing dashboards for customers.
maria: sounds good. creating canary now and tagging @deploy-bot for the rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy request received: canary/telemetry-microtask -> EU canary (10%). ETA 3m.
kevin: ping me when metrics start flowing. I'll watch flamegraphs and main-thread spans.
priya: added exception for early event sampling to avoid losing critical signals when deferred.
alex: FYI I'll also open a follow-up to refactor telemetry so it ships as an independent runtime chunk (so we can control prefetch separately).
maria: thanks. small wins for now — if we see LCP back within threshold I'll mark canary stable and push fix to main. :thumbsup:
jonah: nice coordination. also let's add an instrumentation flag so future telemetry rollouts can be gated at build-time rather than runtime.
maria: noted. I'll update the rollout doc with the experiments and outcome.
kevin: thanks everyone — keep chatter in this thread, and if you see a green/stable signal call it out.
priya: will do, monitoring dashboard link: https://console.internal/redwood/canaries/6481234567
